Nature Communications | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 Fluorine coordination engineering stabilizes amorphous vanadium oxide by converting labile V-O bonds into robust V-F bonds, suppressing vanadium dissolution and water-induced degradation while preserving fast ion transport. This resolves the stability-kinetics trade-off, enabling 155.6 mAh g−1 at 200 A g−1, 70,000-cycle stability, and six-month operation, offering a microscopic-to-macroscopic design principle for practical aqueous zinc batteries.

Angewandte Chemie International Edition | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in revealing a rate-dependent non-equilibrium H3→H2 phase transition during fast discharge (≥4 C) that drives Ni migration and rock-salt collapse in Ni-rich cathodes. Its significance is a practical cycling protocol—a brief low-rate discharge at high voltage—that suppresses phase separation and boosts capacity retention by 29% after 1000 cycles, guiding durable fast-charging battery design.

item.description:

Angewandte Chemie International Edition | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in programming the electric double layer of low-concentration electrolytes via anion solvation behavior, decoupling interfacial stability from high salt use. Large weakly coordinating anions form a persistent shielding layer; small strongly coordinating anions modulate desolvation kinetics. This establishes a mechanistic link between bulk solvation and interfacial organization, offering a design paradigm for efficient electrolyte engineering.

Angewandte Chemie International Edition | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a mixed-valence cobalt-backboned polymer enabling spin-charge cooperative engineering for Li-CO2 batteries. Significance: external magnetic field switches Co from low to high spin, enhancing intervalence charge transfer, CO2 adsorption/activation, and electron transfer to CO2 antibonding orbitals—achieving 1.06 V low overpotential and 2700 h stable cycling, opening avenues for magneto-spin-charge accelerated energy storage.
